test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What was India’s global rank in the aviation market according to the International Aviation Data 2024 report released in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**5th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **International Aviation Data 2024** report released in **2025**, **India** has secured the **5th rank** in the **global aviation market**.
 
• This ranking is a reflection of the total **passenger traffic**, which includes both **domestic** and **international** travelers handled by Indian airports throughout the **calendar year 2024**.
 
• The report highlights that **India** has shown one of the highest **year-on-year growth rates** in the aviation sector, significantly outpacing many developed economies in **Europe**.
 
• Key factors contributing to this **5th position** include the rapid expansion of **low-cost carriers (LCCs)** and the modernization of major **aviation hubs** like **Delhi** and **Mumbai**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 5th.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Domestic Market Standing**: While India is ranked **5th** in the overall global market, it consistently maintains its position as the **3rd largest domestic aviation market** in the world, following the **United States** and **China**.
 
• **UDAN Scheme**: The **Ude Desh Ka Aam Nagrik (UDAN)**, a **Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS)** launched in **October 2016**, has been instrumental in operationalizing **unserved** and **underserved** airports, bringing air travel to **Tier-2** and **Tier-3** cities.
 
• **Fleet Expansion**: Major Indian airlines such as **IndiGo** and **Air India** made global headlines by placing record-breaking orders for over **1,100 aircraft** in recent years, ensuring a steady supply of capacity for future demand.
 
• **Airport Infrastructure**: The number of **operational airports** in India has grown from **74** in **2014** to over **149** by the end of **2024**. The government aims to reach **220 airports** by **2025** through the **National Infrastructure Pipeline**.
 
• **Regulatory Authority**: The **Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA)** is the statutory body of the **Government of India** that regulates civil aviation, focusing on safety issues and **airworthiness** standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Greenfield Airports**: The **Government of India** has accorded 'in-principle' approval for setting up **21 Greenfield Airports** across the country, with major projects like **Noida International Airport (Jewar)** and **Navi Mumbai International Airport** expected to boost capacity significantly.
 
• **Air Cargo Growth**: Beyond passenger travel, India is striving to become a global **cargo hub**. The **Krishi Udan** scheme is a specific initiative designed to assist **farmers** in transporting **perishable agricultural products** to both **domestic** and **international** markets.
 
• **MRO Hub**: India is actively developing as a **Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO)** destination to reduce the dependency on foreign facilities and save **foreign exchange**.
 
• **Digital Initiatives**: The **DigiYatra** initiative, utilizing **Facial Recognition Technology (FRT)**, has been rolled out across several airports to provide a **seamless** and **paperless** entry process for passengers.
</ul
